title: introduce-compact-ci-adapter-and-dep-visibility-gateway
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: our presubmit and lint/test pipelines have accrued a lot of language-specific runners and duplicated setup steps. This PR extracts a small, language-agnostic CI adapter layer (Go) and a lightweight dependency-visibility gateway that centralizes dev-dependency detection, stale-lock telemetry, and a permissive gate for fastpath merges. Goals: reduce presubmit startup time, provide clearer visibility for dep churn, and make staged release hooks less noisy.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds cmd/ci-adapter: a compact Go binary that normalizes workspace bootstrap across languages, caches toolchain leases, and exposes a small HTTP health/sanity endpoint used by GitHub Actions.
- Introduces tooling/dep-visibility: a minimal service (local-only in CI) that computes a dependency surface summary, flags transitive devdeps, and emits a compact dependency fingerprint to a cache key used by staged CI lanes.
- Replaces language-specific presubmit shell fragments in the main workflows with calls to the ci-adapter; reduces duplicated logic in .github/workflows/presubmit-*.yml.
- Adds a presubmit-fastpath label and automation rule: small changes (docs/infra) can skip heavy integration shards when dep-visibility and unit/linters pass.
- Cleans up legacy Makefile targets used only by CI and moves canonical behavior into the adapter.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of ci-adapter and dep-visibility modules
- [x] Replace presubmit workflow fragments and update action inputs
- [x] Add telemetry counters (dep-change-rate, presubmit-latency) to internal CI metrics bridge
- [x] Add docs/ci/README.md describing the adapter and fastpath rules
- [x] Add migration note in docs and small rollout plan

Why this is safe: the adapter is opt-in behind workflow updates; the presubmit workflows are staged behind a rollout flag for the first week. Dep-visibility only influences fastpath gating and does not block default presubmit lanes. Release automation is unchanged in this PR (no artifact signing changes).

Rollout plan: merge to main -> opt-in on small team repos -> enable for core services after 1 week of telemetry. We will monitor presubmit-latency and false skips; rollback by re-enabling legacy fragments if needed.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (presubmit feedback), ENG-4956 (dep surface telemetry).
commits: init: add ci-adapter skeleton and health endpoint
feat(dep-visibility): add dependency fingerprinting and cache integration
chore(ci): swap presubmit fragments to use ./bin/ci-adapter in workflows
docs(ci): add README and migration notes
refactor(make): remove ci-only shorthand targets and reference adapter
review_comments: Aaron Kim: Suggest keeping a short compatibility shim for repos that still invoke make ci locally. Maya: added Makefile targets that forward to the adapter and included migration note.

Lucia Gomez: Can dep-visibility run in parallel with unit tests to avoid adding latency? Maya: yes — the adapter kicks off dep-visibility asynchronously and only waits for its fingerprint when evaluating fastpath rules.
Ravi Shah: Add a feature-flag env var to gate the fastpath behavior during rollout. Maya: added CI_FASTPATH_ENABLED and defaulted to false in workflows; documented rollout steps.
discussion_outcome: Addressed reviewer feedback: compatibility shim, async dep-visibility, rollout flag added; all reviewers approved
release_notes: Introduce a compact CI adapter and a dependency visibility gateway to reduce presubmit duplication and enable a fastpath presubmit lane. Opt-in rollout.
notes_on_testing: Ran presubmit simulations locally and on ephemeral runners. Observed median presubmit bootstrap time drop from ~14s to ~7s for node/python shards. Telemetry hooks exercised in staging for 48h before merge.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Enable CI_FASTPATH_ENABLED=true for core services on 2024-11-25 once telemetry is stable. 2) Remove legacy Makefile CI targets after two weeks. 3) Monitor presubmit-latency and dep-change-rate dashboards.
human_readable_summary: Refactors CI to add a small Go-based adapter and a dependency-visibility component. Reduces duplicate workflow fragments, introduces a safe fastpath for low-risk changes, and standardizes CI bootstrap across languages. Opt-in rollout and telemetry-driven guardrails.
